newsitem.title: UK: UK minutes show no hardening of BOE line - analysts.
newsitem.headline: UK minutes show no hardening of BOE line - analysts.

text.p: Minutes of the September 4 monetary between Bank of England Governor Eddie George and Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke show no significant hardening in the central bank's monetary policy stance, analysts said.
"There is certainly no additional pressure coming from the bank," Jeremy Hawkins of Bank of America told Reuters Financial Television.
"Yes, the bank clearly still wants to see interest rates moving higher but nonetheless I don't think they really stressed any additional calls for higher rates at this meeting."
Marian Bell, economist at Royal Bank of Scotland, said the minutes showed "little firming of the governor's line or increased difference with the chancellor."
"This should prevent any significant gilt and short-sterling negative impact," she said.
Stewart Robertson of Lombard Street Research said George had essentially repeated his message at the July 30 monetary meeting that interest rates should be higher.
"I think he is absolutely right to do that. His mandate is to meet the inflation target and if he sees that under threat, then he should be advocating rate rises," he said.
The minutes showed George calling for a "marginally tighter policy stance now" and warning that the longer a tightening was delayed, the sharper it would need to be.
Hawkins noted that there had been some softer economic data since the previous monetary meeting, including falling manufacturing output and a decline in retail sales.
"Together with the appreciation we saw in the pound...in some ways you could perhaps describe that as a slight tightening in monetary conditions anyway," he said.
